events.location: Clark, SD; Codington, SD; Day, SD; Deuel, SD; Grant, SD; Roberts, SD

details.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northeastern Clark County in northeastern South Dakota...
Codington County in northeastern South Dakota...
Southeastern Day County in northeastern South Dakota...
Northern Deuel County in northeastern South Dakota...
Grant County in northeastern South Dakota...
Southwestern Roberts County in northeastern South Dakota...

* WHEN...Until 830 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 540 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated most of the thunderstorm
activity had ended or moved out of the warned area. However,
flooding is still either ongoing or expected. Between 2 and 5
inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Watertown, Milbank, Big Stone City, Florence, Summit, Rauville,
South Shore, Waverly, Kranzburg, Revillo, Stockholm, Wallace,
Strandburg, Twin Brooks, La Bolt, Ortley, Troy, Marvin and Albee.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.location: Huron; Sanilac; Lapeer; St. Clair; Oakland; Macomb; Wayne; Monroe

details.description:
Areas of dense fog dropping visibilities below 1 mile will exist
for the first half of the morning commute. Fog will gradually
dissipate after sunrise. Drivers should allow extra time and be
prepared for fluctuating visibility.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...In Minnesota, Pine County and Wisconsin, Burnett and
Washburn Counties. This includes the Tribal Lands of the St. Croix
Band in Burnett County and the Mille Lacs Band, Hinckley and, Lena
Lake counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM CDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Very heavy rainfall fell overnight with additional rainfall
possible yet this morning. Areas of minor flooding may occur.
- Flood safety information can be found at
www.weather.gov/safety/flood.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.location: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters

details.description:
Super Typhoon Bavi (09W) is currently centered near 17N133E, roughly
630 miles northwest of Yap and 680 miles north of Palau. Maximum
sustained winds are 155 mph. Yap and Palau continue to face impacts
from elevated northwest swells emanating from STY Bavi and the
trailing monsoon pattern.

Hazardous seas up to 16 feet will continue tonight at Yap, and up to
14 feet at Palau, generated by an elevated northwest swell from STY
Bavi, and from elevated southwest monsoon swell and wind waves.
Surging southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts to 35 knots will
continue tonight, especially near any heavier showers, contributing
to hazardous sea conditions through the next few days. Inter-island
travel will be dangerous. As Bavi continues to pull away toward the
northwest over the next few days, the monsoon pattern will shift
northwest with it, and winds, seas, and surf will gradually subside.
Even so, hazardous surf conditions will continue through at least
Friday afternoon, associated with the elevated swells.

For more information on Super Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the
Public Advisory issued by the National Weather Service under WMO
header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW.

details.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM TO 8 PM MDT THIS AFTERNOON
FOR SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR IDAHO FIRE WEATHER ZONE 427...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 427 Goose Creek and Raft
River Valley/Southern Sawtooth NF/Twin Falls BLM south of the
Snake River.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected to
develop Tuesday. Lightning may generate new fire starts. New
starts may spread rapidly.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Both wet and dry thunderstorms expected with
25 to 35 percent coverage.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts of 30 to 40 mph are possible.

* AFFECTED AREA...Lower Kobuk Valley.

* TIMING...From 10 AM AKDT Wednesday through Wednesday evening.

* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Isolated to Scattered.

* WINDS...West 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* HUMIDITY...As low as 42 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the upper 70s. Lows in the upper 40s.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are possible due to
scattered thunderstorms. Thunderstorms will come with frequent
lightning and outflow boundaries. Any lightning can cause new
ignitions since the fuels are dry and burnable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Westerly sea breezes Wednesday afternoon
will likely limit thunderstorm potential along the coast, with
more concern further east into the upper Kobuk.
